abstract: We study the axisymmetric incompressible Navier--Stokes equations in a finite cylinder subject to the Navier--total--slip boundary condition, that is, the Navier slip condition with zero friction. We prove that the solution remains smooth for all time provided that the initial swirl $\Gamma_0 = r v_{\theta,0}$ has zero mean and an explicit smallness condition on the initial data holds. The condition involves $\Gamma = rv_\theta$ and the variables $V = v_\theta/\sqrt{r}$ and $\Omega = \omega_\theta/r$, and it is invariant under the natural scaling of the Navier--Stokes equations, hence critical. The total-slip condition produces a boundary term on the lateral wall that cannot be controlled by the dissipation alone; we overcome this with a sharp trace-type identity combined with a remainder controlled by $\|\Gamma\|_{L^2}$. In addition, the Robin-type boundary condition $\partial_r \Gamma = 2\Gamma$ destroys the maximum principle for $\Gamma$, and we replace it with a uniform $L^4$ bound. These estimates yield uniform $L^4$ bounds for the velocity, and regularity follows from the Ladyzhenskaya--Prodi--Serrin criterion together with boundary regularity results for the Navier slip condition.
hook: Swirling flow in a cylinder with slippery walls stays smooth forever if its starting swirl is small enough.

summary: The paper proves global smoothness for axisymmetric Navier-Stokes in a finite cylinder with a total-slip wall condition. It handles a boundary term and a lost maximum principle with a trace identity and an L4 bound. The result needs zero-mean swirl and a smallness condition, so it says nothing about large data or the general 3D problem.
title: Global regularity of axisymmetric Navier--Stokes equations under total slip and critical smallness
